name: Lab Inventory
description: Know what you have and where, never run out or let things expire, and make requests and approvals fast. Reagents, consumables, antibodies, cell lines, plasmids and chemicals in one item list with standard and custom categories; lots with quantity, expiry and location in a room → storage unit → shelf or box tree; every quantity change written as a movement; requests that show existing stock first; one approver with an optional amount threshold for a second approver and per-program approvers, never the requester; track-only orders that group requests, with full or partial receiving; "Used one", "Used up" and quick counts from the app or a QR label; reorder suggestions, alerts, QR label sheets (A4 and Letter), spend, waste and stock value reports with CSV, and a concise weekly digest.
whenToUse: A biotech lab's reagents, consumables and research materials: stock, locations, expiry, requests, approvals, order tracking, reorders, spend.
whenNotToUse: Sample tracking (lineage, aliquots, per-tube freezer maps), GMP, GLP or Part 11 inventory, human biospecimens, equipment maintenance or booking, hazard or safety registers, purchasing systems, supplier marketplaces, punch-out or sending purchase orders.

heading.description: App heading shown above every screen.

tableMap.description: JSON object keyed by stable role key: core data contract v1 roles organizations (required, read/write: suppliers), programs and agreements (optional, read only; never created by this app); app roles labinventory.settings, labinventory.categories, labinventory.locations, labinventory.items, labinventory.lots, labinventory.movements, labinventory.requests and labinventory.orders (contract labinventory.v1). Each value is {typeId:<authorized table UUID>, fields:{<logical key>:<real field key>}, writableFields:[<logical keys>]}. Real keys are lowercase snake_case. The installer writes it; never invent table IDs.

pageSize.description: Rows per page in registers (10 to 50).

layoutProfile.description: Stringified native layout profile (heading, tabs, cols, visible) written by the layout gear review. Do not edit by hand.

readOnly.description: Disable every write control in this copy.

demoLabel.description: Label the data as fictional (offline preview only).

asOfOverride.description: Pinned as-of date YYYY-MM-DD for previews and tests. Leave empty in real apps: the app uses today's date.

instructions:
Lab Inventory 2.0.0 is a custom frontend-js app (Vivid kit, theme ocean) for a biotech lab's materials. It replaces Inventory Management 1.0.2 (saved 1.0.2 apps keep working; nothing is migrated). Read read_app_template_guidance (usage, authoring and contracts, every nextOffset; guidance 1.3.25 or later) and read_app_automation_guide before preparing it. Pin life.inventory-management 2.0.0 with its digest. Do not add login, accounts, a shop, punch-out, purchase-order sending or supplier email: orders are tracked only.
INSTALL. Check list_archived_items (kind apps, templateId life.inventory-management) and offer to restore an archived app first. Use installs the app. The Use existing data? dialog connects an existing organizations table by default (core.v1, suppliers; reuse, never copy) and an existing programs or agreements table if there is one (optional, read only; never created). Everything else gets new labinventory.* tables. Assistants may propose choices with prepare_data_access and never confirm them. No records are seeded: the six standard categories (Reagent, Consumable, Antibody, Cell line, Plasmid, Chemical) are added with one click in Reports & settings, and the standard units are built in.
SET-UP. Reports & settings: approver (required; usually the lab manager), optional second approver above a threshold amount, optional approver per program, currency; add the standard categories and your own (for example Primers); units; the app link (copy it from the browser address bar) so QR labels open the item page; expiry window (30 days) and the digest cadence (weekly, Monday 08:00), recipients and text. Locations: rooms, then freezers, fridges and cabinets, then shelves and boxes. Inventory: items (category, supplier, catalog number, unit, last price, reorder point, usual order quantity, lead time, default location, program).
DAILY USE. "You" at the top names the person; it is recorded on requests, approvals and use. Requests: a new request shows lots already in stock and open requests for the same item before it is submitted. Approve, reject with a reason, or ask a question; the approver is the program approver if set, else the approver; above the threshold the second approver approves next; the requester can never approve their own request (the next approver is used). Orders: approved requests are grouped by supplier; log one order for several requests (supplier, order number, date, expected date, amount); receive in full or in part, creating one lot per line with lot number, expiry and location; then record the received movements (one click: the platform gives a lot its ID when it is created, so its received movement follows in the next review). Inventory and the QR item page: "Used one" takes one unit from the earliest-expiring lot, "Used up" empties a lot, a quick count sets the real quantity and logs the difference, Move changes the location, Discard counts waste. Every lot quantity change is written with a movement in the same review.
CALCULATIONS. Stock = sum of in_stock lot quantities; low when stock <= reorder_point. Suggested quantity = reorder_quantity if set, else average use per day over the last 90 days of used movements x (lead_time_days + 14), rounded up; no suggestion without usage and reorder quantity. Expiring: expires_on within the window; expired: past expires_on and still in stock. Waste = discarded or expired quantity x last price per month. Spend = order amounts by ordered month, supplier and program, split by request (estimated amount, else equally). Stock value = in-stock quantity x last price. Amounts in another currency than the settings currency are listed apart, never summed.
ASSISTANTS. Turn what the user gives (chat, pasted order confirmations, label photos, lists) into proposed records with prepare_change; check existing stock and duplicates first (read the items and lots). Receiving from a confirmation: propose a new labinventory.items record for an unknown product first; after it is confirmed, propose the lots (item_id, lot_number, quantity, expires_on, location_id, received_on, status in_stock, order_id) with the order status update, then one received movement per lot (kind received, quantity_change = quantity, via assistant). Use from chat ("we used 3 boxes of tips"): one bulk_records proposal that updates the earliest-expiring in-stock lot's quantity (and status used_up at 0) and creates the used movement (quantity_change -3, via assistant). Requests from chat: a labinventory.requests record with status requested, requested_by the person, never approval fields. Suggest reorders and summarise spend. Never set approved_1_by, approved_2_by, decision_on or reject_reason, never set status approved, rejected or cancelled, never confirm a review, never contact suppliers, never make safety or regulatory claims. Owners can enforce this with Database column rules that deny Claude and ChatGPT writes to the approval fields.
AUTOMATIONS (all optional; see documentation.tasks). Never activate one the user did not ask for.
RECOVERY. Partial reads disable writes with a banner. A stale review is rejected with the draft kept; reopen and submit again.

quickStart: Read the current usage, authoring and contracts guidance and this documentation; pin life.inventory-management 2.0.0 and its digest with one requestKey.

Check for an archived Lab Inventory app and offer to restore it. Otherwise Use installs it; keep the default that connects an existing organizations table (suppliers), and programs or agreements tables when they exist.

Reports & settings: set the approver (and optionally the second approver, threshold and program approvers), add the standard categories, paste the app link for QR codes, check the expiry window and digest.
Locations: add rooms, storage units and shelves or boxes. Inventory: add items, or ask the assistant to propose them from a list.
Print QR labels for items and shelves (A4 or Letter). Requests, approvals, orders, receiving and use then run from the app, the QR page or the assistant.
Optionally set up the weekly digest and the approval and status emails in TrialAgents → Automations.
documentation.dataContract: Stable role keys; every field scalar (multiple false), lowercase snake_case, relationships by record ID in text fields. Core data contract v1: organizations (required, read/write; suppliers with org_type other or partner: name*, org_type, country, website, archived), programs (optional, read only: name*, code, stage*, status, archived), agreements (optional, read only, core fields: name*, counterparty_id, agreement_type, status, effective_date, expiry_date, archived). App tables, contract labinventory.v1: labinventory.settings (one row: approver*, second_approver, threshold_amount, currency EUR, program_approvers JSON {programId:name}, expiry_window_days 30, digest_cadence daily/weekly/monthly weekly, digest_day mon..sun mon, digest_time 08:00, digest_recipients, digest_text, units comma list, app_link), labinventory.categories (name*, standard, archived), labinventory.locations (name*, parent_id, kind* room/freezer/fridge/cabinet/shelf/box/other, temperature, archived), labinventory.items (name*, category_id*, supplier_id, catalog_number, unit*, unit_size, last_price, currency, reorder_point, reorder_quantity, lead_time_days, default_location_id, program_id, owner, notes, archived), labinventory.lots (item_id*, lot_number, quantity*, received_on, expires_on, location_id*, owner, status* in_stock/used_up/expired/discarded, order_id), labinventory.movements (lot_id*, kind* received/used/count/moved/discarded, quantity_change* signed, occurred_on*, by, via app/qr/assistant, note), labinventory.requests (item_id, item_name, new_item_name, quantity*, program_id, urgency normal/urgent, estimated_amount, requested_by*, requested_on*, status* requested/approved/rejected/ordered/received/cancelled, approved_1_by, approved_2_by, decision_on, reject_reason, order_id, note), labinventory.orders (supplier_id*, order_number, ordered_by*, ordered_on*, expected_on, amount, currency, status* ordered/partially_received/received/cancelled, request_ids comma list, notes). * = required. Lot quantity changes always write a movement. orders.request_ids is authoritative for which requests an order holds. A request counts as approved only with approved_1_by (not the requester) and, above threshold_amount, approved_2_by (another person); otherwise it is shown as "approval invalid" and cannot be ordered. Lab Inventory never writes another app's own tables and never writes programs or agreements. Display names are read from the records; IDs are never shown.
documentation.interactionContract: Six screens with stable IDs for the native layout gear: overview, inventory, requests, orders, locations, settings, plus the mobile item page (item) opened from a QR label (route /item with recordId) or from an item; column groups items and requests. Details open in the side panel. Overview: alerts (low stock, expiring in the window, expired, approvals waiting, late orders), suggested reorders with one-click requests, my requests with status, spend this month by program. Inventory: search and filters (category, location, supplier, program, status), item panel with lots (quantity, expiry, location, owner, earliest-expiring marked), Used one / Used up / Count / Move / Discard, usage history, past orders and prices, Add item, Add lot, QR labels. Requests: status flow, approval queue with amount and second-approver flags, new request with the stock check, review panel to approve, reject with a reason, ask a question or cancel (requester). Orders: approved requests by supplier, log order for several requests, supplier agreements from Contracts, receive full or partial, late orders, history. Locations: tree, contents, add inside, QR label, archive empty locations. Reports & settings: spend by program, supplier and month, expiry waste, stock value, CSV export text; categories; units and the QR app link; approvals; alerts and digest with a preview of the exact digest text. Every write is one records.propose shown in the TrialAgents review; drafts are kept in state on change (data-ui-state on every input). Label sheets render A4 (21 labels) or Letter (10 labels) for the browser's print; custom apps cannot open a print dialog or a download.
documentation.lifecycle: A new preview shows empty or fictional data and never writes. Saved apps re-read their tables and configuration on every render (bounded reads: 100 rows a page, up to 800 rows per table; movements newest first). Record writes are records.propose batches (at most 50 per review) confirmed in the TrialAgents review; a stale version is rejected with the draft kept. Receiving and Add lot are two reviews (lots, then their received movements) because a record gets its ID when it is created; the app shows the pending movements until they are recorded. Layout changes are reviewed presentation-only edits. Archive first: items, categories and locations are archived (never deleted); archiving the app keeps every table and record and pauses its automations, which come back switched off when the app is restored.
limitations: Orders are tracked only: no supplier marketplace, punch-out, purchase-order sending, purchasing or accounting integration.
No GMP, GLP or Part 11 controls, human biospecimens, full sample tracking, equipment booking or hazard registers.

The app knows people by the name entered under "You", not by sign-in identity; the TrialAgents review log records who confirmed each change. Database column rules can deny assistants writes to the approval fields.
Label sheets and CSV are shown in the app for the browser's print and for copying; custom apps cannot start a print dialog or a file download yet. QR codes need the app link in Settings.
Receiving creates lots in one review and their received movements in the next.
Reads are bounded (800 rows per table); beyond that the app shows partial data and disables writes, except for very long movement histories, which only shorten usage averages.

examples.prompt: Here is the order confirmation from Example Reagents: 2 × FBS lot 24B117 expiring 03/2027, 6 × DMEM lot D8812 expiring 05/2027, and a new item, Primer set NWB-202 (3 tubes, lot P-0091, expiry 11/2027). Put it in.
examples.expectedBehavior: Finds the open order and its requests, checks existing items, proposes the new labinventory.items record first; after it is confirmed, proposes three lots (location from each item's default, received_on today, order_id) with the order status (received or partially_received) and request updates, then the three received movements. Nothing is confirmed by the assistant.

examples.prompt: We used 3 boxes of 200 µL tips.
examples.expectedBehavior: Reads the tips' lots, picks the earliest-expiring in-stock lot, and proposes one review: the lot quantity minus 3 (used_up at 0) and a used movement of -3 via assistant. If no lot has 3 left it splits across lots or asks.

examples.prompt: Order more ethanol and gloves, and tell me what we spent on NWB-101 last quarter.
examples.expectedBehavior: Checks stock and open requests, proposes requests (status requested, requested_by the user, suggested quantities per the reorder rule) and summarises spend from labinventory.orders split by request program. Never approves or contacts the supplier.

examples.prompt: Approve Ana's request for the ELISA kits.
examples.expectedBehavior: Explains that assistants never approve: the approver opens the request in Lab Inventory → Requests and approves it there.

tasks.whenUseful: Three optional automations; the app never waits for one and works fully without them. (1) Weekly digest: a research worker on the user's Claude or ChatGPT runner, calendar trigger from the settings (weekly default, Monday 08:00 in the workspace time zone; daily or monthly as set), runs the app with run_component_frontend (request {componentId:<Lab Inventory app ID>, state:{section:"settings"}, event:{kind:"open"}}) and returns the text of the block marked data-digest verbatim as the run summary; a separate TrialAgents email action with trigger database, source automation_runs, that research automation and status becoming completed sends {{run.summary}} to the chosen members. The digest lists low stock, suggested reorders, expiring and expired lots, approvals waiting and late orders, at most 3 lines per section, empty sections omitted (one line when nothing needs attention). (2) Approval request: a TrialAgents email action on labinventory.requests entry creation to the approver (a registered member with app access), text with {{record.item_name}}, {{record.quantity}}, {{record.requested_by}} and {{record.estimated_amount}}; in-app the approver sees the queue. (3) Status updates: for a requester who wants email, one TrialAgents email action per status they want (approved, rejected, ordered, received): database trigger on labinventory.requests updates with status becoming that value and the condition requested_by equals that person, text with {{record.item_name}} and {{record.status}}; in-app everyone sees the status on Requests and Overview.
tasks.readRequirements: Digest: the app's bound tables through run_component_frontend under the runner's app access (no other reads). Emails: the request record fields named in the text.
tasks.outputContract: Digest research writes no records; its result is the summary text only. Emails are TrialAgents emails to explicitly selected registered members with current app access; no supplier or outside address is ever emailed. Dedup: one digest per scheduled occurrence; one email per request creation or status change.
tasks.promptExample: Run Lab Inventory with run_component_frontend (request {componentId:"<app id>", state:{section:"settings"}, event:{kind:"open"}}). Copy the text inside the <pre> element marked data-digest exactly, without adding or removing anything, and finish the run with that text as the summary. Do not read other sources, write records, approve anything or contact anyone. If the app cannot be run or shows a partial-data banner, finish as failed with the reason. Without an automation, open Reports & settings to read the same digest.
